title: Evaluating and Improving LLM Self-Modeling
abstract: arXiv:2608.30980v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study self-modeling: an LLM's ability to answer questions about its own behavior. We focus on verifiable behavioral questions, such as whether a prompt edit would change the model's final answer. To measure this capability, we introduce a benchmark that tests diverse types of self-modeling questions. Current models show non-trivial but limited self-modeling skill, and make systematic mistakes on simple counterfactual questions about their own behavior. To improve self-modeling skill, we develop a scalable synthetic-data pipeline that produces self-modeling training data, and show that reinforcement-learning can improve aggregate self-modeling skill across three open-source model families with some transfer to held-out tasks. These gains, however, do not seem to constitute introspection consistently: improved self-modeling may not arise from privileged access to the model's internal decision process.

translated_title: 评估与改进大语言模型的自我建模能力
translated_abstract: 我们研究自我建模：即大语言模型回答关于自身行为问题的能力。我们聚焦于可验证的行为类问题，例如对提示词的修改是否会改变模型的最终答案。为了衡量这种能力，我们引入了一个测试多种类型自我建模问题的基准。当前模型表现出不容忽视但有限的自我建模能力，并且在关于自身行为的简单反事实问题上会犯系统性错误。为了提升自我建模能力，我们开发了一个可扩展的合成数据流水线来生成自我建模训练数据，并证明强化学习可以提升三个开源模型家族的整体自我建模能力，且在一定程度上能够迁移到留出的任务上。然而，这些提升似乎并不总是构成真正的内省：自我建模能力的改进可能并非源于模型对自身内部决策过程的特殊访问权限。
tldr: 本文提出了评估大语言模型自我建模能力的基准，发现当前模型该能力有限且在反事实问题上存在系统性错误，并通过合成数据流水线与强化学习提升了三个开源模型家族的自我建模能力，但这些提升可能并非源于真正的内省。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating LLM self-modeling, finds that current models show limited skill with systematic errors on simple counterfactual questions, and improves self-modeling across three open-source model families via a scalable synthetic-data pipeline and reinforcement learning, though these gains may not constitute genuine introspection.
